quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A train has passed at a railroad crossing. What should you do next?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not go forward until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather so you can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
One car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too close to a truck, the driver cannot see you. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety space if the vehicle stops suddenly.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors often while driving. This helps you know where vehicles near you are located.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A side road is coming ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is coming ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a side road will cross ahead.

questions.question: Oncoming cars are on your left and parked cars are on your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming cars than the parked cars.
Closer to the parked cars than the oncoming cars.
Down the middle between the oncoming and parked cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between the oncoming and parked cars.
questions.explanation: When trapped between oncoming traffic and parked cars, steer down the middle. This gives you the most space away from both sides.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to any driver who:
questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you did.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, drivers should go in the order they arrived. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be unsafe.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates drivers behind you and causes them to make risky passes. Drive with traffic flow, within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does an orange and red triangle sign on a vehicle always mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. You cannot turn right at an intersection with this sign.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your car and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles towing trailers cannot see you if you are directly behind them. Stay farther back from these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so extra distance helps you see around them.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Disappear in blind spots or are so close they prevent the truck from stopping and turning safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear in blind spots or are so close they prevent the truck from stopping and turning safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas where cars disappear into a truck or bus's blind spots. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Dangerous only if you have a helper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Use extra care when backing up.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines on a two-lane road mean any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Drive through carefully and do not slow down to look at the activity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through carefully and do not slow down to look at the activity.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at construction activity. This causes traffic to back up. Keep moving through the zone at a safe speed.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are going. They may be moving faster than they appear. Make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle passes and you have clear space to change lanes safely.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and cold showers do not speed this up.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, you should be able to clearly see:
questions.correctAnswerText: The entire rear window.
questions.explanation: Set your rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window from the driver's seat. You should only need to move your eyes, not your head, to use this mirror.

questions.question: Your vehicle wheels have gone off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get the car back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, grip the steering wheel firmly, lift your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Slow down before trying to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly, as this can cause you to lose control or move into other traffic.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the traffic around you, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly during heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you slow traffic and block normal movement, you can get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless traffic exceeds the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already inside it.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not enough sleep causes poor driving. Sleepiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and damages your judgment, just like drugs and alcohol do.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol level nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: The left lane nearest the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane nearest the curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder, hitting you.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a stop sign is coming.
